claim: Of the 69,000 bureaux de vote in the INSEE REU, 3,000 (approximately 4.3%) have identifiers that differ between the REU and the Ministry of Interior's information system that centralizes election results, as of the September 2022 REU extraction.
stance_target: French bureau-de-vote crosswalk is not perfectly stable; direct quantification of ID mismatch rate
scope_conditions: REU extraction of September 2022, joined against the Ministry of Interior's SIE (système d'information élections)
quoted_support: Il subsiste toutefois quelques cas (3 000 bureaux de vote sur 69 000), où ces identifiants sont différents.
numbers: 3,000 of 69,000 bureaux de vote (~4.3%) with mismatched IDs

claim: The INSEE/Etalab bureau-de-vote ID crosswalk was constructed via a multi-step manual/automated cascade, not a single deterministic join: a first cleaned-index join matched ~66,000/69,000 bureaux (~95.6%), arrondissement-specific Ministry conversion rules recovered ~1,600 more in Paris/Lyon/Marseille, systematic single-bureau-per-commune matching recovered ~400, and eyeballed manual matching of 'obvious' sequential-code patterns recovered a further ~300 — after which ~130 REU-side and ~250 Ministry-side bureaux remained permanently unmatched.
stance_target: concrete mechanics of how table-bv-reu-style crosswalks are built, showing heavy reliance on manual/heuristic steps rather than a stable coding norm
scope_conditions: September 2022 REU extraction, joined against Ministry of Interior election results system
quoted_support: Jointure classique sur les indices construits, ce qui met en concordance la majorité des bureaux de vote (~66k sur un total de 69k de bureaux dans le REU) ... Association manuelle des bureaux de vote des 2 fichiers lorsque le rapprochement est « évident »
time_period: work completed by June 2023, based on September 2022 REU extraction

claim: The residual unmatched bureaux de vote after the full matching cascade are concentrated in three named communes — Belfort, Troyes, and Dieppe — where the bureau-code indices on each side of the crosswalk cannot be reconciled with certainty, attributed by INSEE/Etalab to bureaux being split into two on one side but not the other, or to commune boundary changes.
stance_target: bureau splits/merges and commune boundary changes are the concrete mechanism behind cross-election ID mismatch, not just formatting quirks
scope_conditions: September 2022 REU extraction vs Ministry of Interior results system
quoted_support: Une grande partie de ces rebuts sont localisés dans 3 communes : Belfort, Troyes et Dieppe, pour lesquelles les indices des bureaux de vote de chaque côté ne permettent pas de faire d'association avec certitude. Pour les autres, il s'agit peut-être de bureaux de vote divisés en deux d'un côté et pas de l'autre ou bien de changements de communes.

claim: INSEE and Etalab explicitly disclaim the bureau-de-vote correspondence table as unofficial, experimental, one-off ('ponctuelle'), and not reliable at 100%, and warn that the underlying referentials can change over time such that the correspondence work is only valid for the specific data considered at the time it was built.
stance_target: the crosswalk is not a maintained, versioned, per-cycle-updated official artifact but a point-in-time experimental product
scope_conditions: as documented June 2023, applying to the September 2022 REU extraction
quoted_support: Ces correspondances ne revêtent aucun caractère officiel et ne sont qu'un travail expérimental conjoint entre l'Insee et Etalab... Elle n'est donc pas fiable à 100%... le travail effectué n'est pertinent que pour les données considérées, les différents référentiels pouvant changer avec le temps.

claim: The bureau-de-vote matching index is built as {code_commune}_{code_du_bv_dans_la_commune}, with cleaning that strips special characters and leading zeros, and requires bespoke commune-code conversion rules for French overseas territories (excluding Saint-Martin and Saint-Barthélemy) provided by the Ministry of Interior — indicating the join key itself is not a stable, self-describing identifier but a constructed composite requiring per-source normalization rules.
stance_target: mechanics of the bureau-ID join key construction, showing fragility/complexity even before considering redistricting churn
quoted_support: Constitution d'un indice de bureau de vote comme {code_commune}_{code_du_bv_dans_la_commune} des 2 côtés, suivi d'un nettoyage standard sur les codes des bureaux (notamment retirer les caractères spéciaux et les leading zeros). Pour les collectivités d'outre-mer (hors Saint-Martin et Saint-Barthélémy), conversion des codes communes selon les indications du ministère de l'Intérieur.

claim: The REU itself is continuously updated ('mis à jour en permanence'), and a single extracted row corresponds to a distinct (attachment address, bureau de vote) pair rather than a distinct voter, meaning bureau-de-vote assignment data drawn from any REU snapshot is inherently a point-in-time cut of a live-changing register rather than a fixed periodic release.
stance_target: temporal stability of REU as a data source for bureau-level analysis
quoted_support: Les lignes du fichier brut correspond aux couples (adresse de rattachement, bureau de vote) distincts dans le Répertoire Électoral Unique, ce dernier étant mis à jour en permanence.
